reported.title: Fan stays ON after boost release below OFF threshold
reported.description: The boost branch at lines 62-67 calls driveFan(true) and resets offHold to 0 every sample while D4 is LOW, but on release the hysteresis logic at lines 78-94 requires offHold to reach HOLD (4 samples, ~200 ms) before turning the fan off. Because offHold was zeroed during the press, the fan lingers ON after the button is released even though tempC is below OFF_C, producing the measured 'D5 was not LOW for 300 ms while required' at 551 ms. D5 was in the wrong state for 444 ms across 3 interval(s), first at 551 ms: D5 was not LOW for 300 ms while required (grace 500 ms).

reported.title: No debounce or rate limiting on boost button causes excessive fan toggles
reported.description: The boost input is read directly at line 62 with no debounce and no minimum on/off dwell or toggle-rate limiter, so each bounce edge or rapid press drives driveFan(true) at line 66 and the subsequent offHold rebuild at lines 78-94 drives driveFan(false), toggling D5 far more than twice per 5000 ms. Measured evidence shows 7 toggles (bounce), 8 toggles (short presses), and 26 toggles (rapid presses) in a 5000 ms window against a limit of 2. D5 toggled 7 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 1.00 s (limit 2), and 8 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

judge_input.spec:
- Temperature probe on A3 at 10 mV/°C; loft fan relay on D5; boost pushbutton on D4 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Turn the fan ON at 36.0 °C or above; turn it OFF at 32.0 °C or below.
- While D4 is held LOW, force the fan ON.
- Fan must not change state more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
- Print `loft: <temp> C fan=ON` or `loft: <temp> C fan=OFF` every 1000 ms.
- Apply fan changes within 500 ms of a sustained threshold crossing.
